rationale: The source bundles three obligations with different activations and evidence. (1) A WMBT on a MAPPED dimension+direction must carry an executable bar naming the table's metric_id: subject is a WMBT, checked by the SMOKE validator over the whole corpus (including unchanged WMBTs), advisory. (2) A WMBT on a deliberately UNMAPPED pair (effort/frequency upward) must state its own metric instead of inheriting a default: same reader, but a different Given, no validator selection, no threshold requirement and no prescribed location for the metric. (3) The dimension->metric table itself must stay total over wmbt.schema.json's 24 dimension x direction pairs, keyed at the schema's spelling, synonyms resolved alike, every no-default pair marked `unmapped` with a reason: subject is the table/schema, not a WMBT, pinned by a different test. The previous single rewrite failed because one THEN could not carry the WMBT bar and the table-maintenance branch together (activation TOO_NARROW) and weakened 'executable bar' to field presence. Parts 1 and 2 jointly cover every pair a WMBT can carry (S006: mapped OR explicitly unmapped), so they require each other; both follow part 3, whose totality guarantees nothing falls through between them. Round 2: part 2 no longer mandates that the own metric sit in an acceptance (S061 only requires the WMBT to state it).

parts.given: A WMBT under plan/ has a dimension+direction that the dimension->metric table maps to a metric_id.
parts.when: You create or edit that WMBT or its acceptances, or the SMOKE corpus check inspects it (unchanged WMBTs included).
parts.then: An acceptance states an executable bar: signal.metric equal to the table's metric_id for that pair, plus a signal.threshold that can be evaluated.
prefer: Table, down (minimize|decrease) / up (maximize|increase), all metric:-prefixed: time latency_p50/latency_increase; effort user_steps/unmapped; likelihood error_ratio/success_ratio; frequency occurrence_rate/unmapped; quantity scrap_rate/throughput; financial value cost_per_unit/net_margin.
Use the schema's exact dimension/direction spelling; minimize=decrease and maximize=increase resolve to the same metric_id.
Copy the metric_id verbatim, metric: prefix included.
avoid: A mapped-pair WMBT with no bar, a metric other than the table's, a threshold that cannot be evaluated, or a bar dropped on edit.
Reading 'advisory' as permission never to add the bar — the debt is paid deliberately, in phases.
parts.why: A dimension+direction is testable only once it names a metric and an evaluable threshold; of 368 mapped WMBTs, none did.
evidence: Validator test_metric_mapping_corpus_drift::test_mapped_wmbts_without_an_executable_bar_are_reported lists mapped WMBTs lacking a bar, with failure evidence wmbt_urn, dimension, direction, metric_id, cause.

Reviewer traverses wmbt file -> acceptances[] -> signal.metric / signal.threshold and confirms signal.metric equals the table's metric_id and the threshold is a bar passes() can evaluate (not just a present field).
verifier_detail: Dimension->direction->metric_id table: time: minimize/decrease -> metric:latency_p50, maximize/increase -> metric:latency_increase; effort: minimize/decrease -> metric:user_steps, maximize/increase -> unmapped; likelihood: minimize/decrease -> metric:error_ratio, maximize/increase -> metric:success_ratio; frequency: minimize/decrease -> metric:occurrence_rate, maximize/increase -> unmapped; quantity: minimize/decrease -> metric:scrap_rate, maximize/increase -> metric:throughput; financial value: minimize/decrease -> metric:cost_per_unit, maximize/increase -> metric:net_margin. Example from the statement: time/minimize -> metric:latency_p50.

Direction synonyms: the direction enum carries two spellings of each intent; downward = [minimize, decrease] ('less of this is better'); upward = [maximize, increase] ('more of this is better'). A dimension resolves both spellings of one intent to the same metric_id. Before #1959 it did not, and 102 of 472 authored WMBTs mapped to nothing because they wrote `minimize` where the table had `decrease`.

Validation: family presence; template required_field_presence; variant planner_criteria_metric_mapping_corpus; phase SMOKE; enforcement advisory; subject_kind wmbt; selector: WMBT files under plan/ whose dimension+direction this node maps to a metric_id; traversal: wmbt file -> acceptances[] -> signal.metric / signal.threshold; invariant: a WMBT the mapping covers states an executable bar naming the metric_id the mapping assigns it; failure_evidence: wmbt_urn, dimension, direction, metric_id, cause.

Why advisory (severity 2): all 368 mapped WMBTs would fail on day one, and the remedy is not yet affordable because no error_ratio, success_ratio or occurrence_rate module exists for runners/metric_runner.py to resolve; the validator reports a count and lets the debt be paid deliberately (issue Decision #2: phase it, never fail 368 at once).
Before #1925 a threshold reaching passes() was stringified and every comparison swallowed, so binding this node would have enforced a bar that was never evaluated; that constraint is gone.

Corpus baseline (source note): over 472 WMBTs, 368 carry a dimension+direction this table maps and NOT ONE states an executable bar; the single bar in the corpus (govern_lifecycle/D010) is quantity/minimize, which the source note says this table does not map.

parts.given: A WMBT under plan/ has effort or frequency with direction maximize or increase — a pair the table marks `unmapped`.
parts.when: You create or edit that WMBT.
parts.then: The WMBT states its own metric instead of inheriting a table default.
prefer: Treat the WMBT as legal: an unmapped pair is a deliberate omission, not an error.
Remember the synonyms: effort/increase and frequency/increase are unmapped exactly like their maximize forms.
avoid: Inheriting a default — including the dimension's downward metric (metric:user_steps, metric:occurrence_rate) reused for the upward intent.
parts.why: No upward metric was ever chosen for effort or frequency; their only defaults are downward, so there is nothing valid to inherit.
evidence: Reviewer confirms the WMBT states its own metric and does not rely on a table default; this rule prescribes neither where the metric is stated nor a threshold.
Not selected by test_metric_mapping_corpus_drift: its selector covers only WMBTs whose pair maps to a metric_id.
verifier_detail: Unmapped pairs = those carrying the `unmapped` sentinel in dimension_metric, each with the reason it has no default. effort/maximize: no upward default — metric:user_steps counts steps and the criteria vocabulary optimises for fewer; no metric was ever chosen for wanting more effort. effort/increase: no upward default; same as effort/maximize, its synonym. frequency/maximize: no upward default — metric:occurrence_rate is paired with the downward intent, the rate of an occurrence you want less of; no metric was chosen for an occurrence you want more of. frequency/increase: no upward default; same as frequency/maximize, its synonym.

Every unmapped dimension names a downward metric only; the table's other dimensions pair each intent with a DIFFERENT metric (error_ratio vs success_ratio, scrap_rate vs throughput, cost_per_unit vs net_margin), so an upward default cannot be the downward metric reused — it would have to be a metric never chosen.
A WMBT on one of these pairs is legal and must state its own metric rather than inherit a default.
The `unmapped` sentinel plus a stated reason lets a reader tell a deliberate omission from a missing row.
Corpus carriers: effort/maximize by wmbt:implement-code:E001; frequency/maximize by wmbt:integrate-end-to-end:M001.

The schema owns both vocabularies — key the table at its exact spelling. Statement: each dimension+direction maps to a default metric_id or is explicitly declared unmapped; the table is total over the enums; nothing falls through it silently.
